To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a bead‐based affinity chromatography system that can be integrated into a glass silicon microchip.

we developed a microbead affinity purification system, which is based on a photolytic elusion method, for the purification and identification of specific target protein from a protein mixture on a microchip.
we have developed an efficient microbeads‐based affinity chromatography system on a glass‐silicone microchip.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method for protein purification and detection on a microchip.
the development of a microaffinity chromatography on a bead chip that can be integrated with a microchip for the purification of proteins based upon photolytic elusion.
the development of a new type of affinity chromatography on chip, which is based on the photolysis of a covalent bond between the affinity ligand and a solid support, such as beads.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this system is a promising approach to develop a high‐throughput and low‐cost microchip‐based protein purification system.
the microaffinity purification system is a promising approach toward a high‐sensitive protein chip for diagnosis.
the microbead affinity purification on a chip is a useful tool for the purification of specific proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the microaffinity chromatography system, based on photolytically eluted CutiCore® bead, was successfully integrated into the glass‐silicon chip, and it can provide a simple and efficient method for the identification and purification of target proteins from a complex protein mixture.
the microaffinity purification system is useful for the identification of target proteins and the development of diagnosis chips.

we developed the microaffinity purification system, which was integrated into a microchip, and demonstrated that this system could be used for the identification of target protein in a protein mixture and for the detection of specific target protein in human serum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microaffinity system can be used as a diagnostic tool to detect the presence of a specific target protein from a protein mixture.
the photolytic release of the target protein from the affinity beads in the filter chamber of the microchip can be used to identify specific target proteins.
